title: PostgreSQL frontend/backend protocol
summary: PostgreSQL's wire protocol is a message-based TCP protocol. Each message: 1-byte type (for frontend messages; backend messages have a type byte too), 4-byte length (including itself), then payload. Startup: SSL request (optional), StartupMessage (protocol version 3.0 + parameters), Authentication (md5/scram), then ReadyForQuery. Queries: SimpleQuery ('Q' + SQL string) or Extended Query (Parse/Bind/Execute/Sync).

structure.meaning: Frontend: 'Q' (query), 'P' (parse), 'B' (bind), 'E' (execute), 'S' (sync), 'X' (terminate), 'p' (password). Backend: 'R' (auth), 'S' (parameter status), 'K' (backend key), 'Z' (ready for query), 'T' (row description), 'D' (data row), 'C' (command complete), 'E' (error), 'N' (notice).
Message length including the length field itself (big-endian).
Message-specific data (SQL string, bind parameters, row values, etc.).
Protocol version (0x00030000 for v3.0) + null-terminated key-value pairs (user, database, application_name, ...).
Number of columns (int16) + for each: column length (int32, -1 for NULL) + column data bytes.
SASL mechanism names (e.g. 'SCRAM-SHA-256') + NUL. Followed by SASL challenge/response.

notes: PostgreSQL uses a binary protocol with type OIDs for column values.
Extended query protocol (Parse/Bind/Execute) supports prepared statements and parameter binding.
COPY protocol (COPY IN/OUT) streams bulk data in a binary or text format.
SCRAM-SHA-256 is the default authentication method (replacing md5).
Logical replication uses a separate protocol (pgoutput) over replication slots.
